title: Inclusive Community Policy adopted; veterans' crosswalk report ordered
subtitle: Also: Douglas Crescent watermain tender, Centre Wellington Energy changes, deputy clerk appointment, provincial legislation update, Elora Festival and Sustainable Waterloo Region presentations.
overview: Council adopted an Inclusive Community Policy that sets one process for requests to fly flags, light public spaces, use public display screens and add dates to a township diversity calendar. It replaces the Municipal Flag Policy on June 1, 2026. The policy was adopted {{vote:m9}}.

After hearing from three Royal Canadian Legion delegates, council directed staff to prepare a comprehensive report on veterans' painted crosswalks. Staff are to consult the County of Wellington and the Elora and Fergus Legion branches. The direction passed {{vote:m10}}. The policy does not mention crosswalks, so it does not block them.

Council awarded the Douglas Crescent watermain contract in Fergus for $1,052,620.87 and revised the funding {{vote:m12}}. After the closed session, council also adopted a business case study on amending the articles of incorporation for Centre Wellington Energy Inc. {{vote:m3}}. It appointed Rachel Cannon as Deputy Municipal Clerk through a consent item and by-law 2026-32. Council received a legislative update on Bills 98 and 100 and the Canada-Ontario Partnership to Build for information {{vote:m11}}.

decisions.detail: Council authorized a by-law adopting the Inclusive Community Policy, which replaces the Municipal Flag Policy effective June 1, 2026.
Staff are directed to prepare a comprehensive report on veterans' painted crosswalks, in consultation with the County of Wellington and the Elora and Fergus Legion branches.
Request for Tender #25-26 was awarded to James Thoume Construction Ltd. at $1,052,620.87, including contingency and non-rebate HST, with funding revised per report FIN2026-02.

decisions.item: Centre Wellington Energy Inc. business case study
decisions.detail: Council adopted the business case study on amending the company's Articles of Incorporation and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign the sole shareholder's special resolution.
Council approved the consent items, including the appointment of Rachel Cannon as Deputy Municipal Clerk, and passed the enabling by-law separately.
Council received the staff report on provincial and federal legislative and funding changes affecting planning for information.

debate: Legion delegates said veterans should not be grouped with other interest groups in a policy. They said crosswalks honour veterans every day, not only on November 11, and noted that other communities, including Guelph, have installed them. One delegate offered the Elora branch's help with up to $500 a year for upkeep, if requested annually.

Staff said the policy never mentions crosswalks, so it does not prevent them. Councillors agreed to deal with the policy and the crosswalk separately instead of excluding veterans from the policy or adding crosswalks to it. One councillor pointed out that veterans could still be recognized through illumination and display screens.

One councillor, who sits on the inclusion committee, said the earlier concerns about crosswalks were about feasibility and paint as a possible distraction, and were not meant as disrespect to veterans. Another councillor raised more durable products such as thermoplastic, with snowplow damage as a concern.

A councillor questioned the proposed lighting and video screen costs. Staff said the lighting funds would centralize existing bridge lighting with building lighting, and the screens would be permanent in public reception areas.

On the legislative update, staff said Bill 98 would let landowners self-identify parkland, possibly including encumbered lands, and would remove sustainable design from site plan control. Staff said enhanced standards might still be possible under a community planning permit system. Details on development-charge funding were limited.
